newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sugar body cuts beet delivery forecast.
newsitem.headline: German sugar body cuts beet delivery forecast.

text.p: German sugar industry association WVZ reduced its forecast for final beet deliveries in the 1996/97 campaign to 25.80 million tonnes, down from 26.43 million estimated up to last week.
A WVZ official said the onset of winter weather and rain in some regions had made harvesting difficult as tractors got stuck in wet fields and night frosts endangered plants in the ground.
But more than two thirds of the crop had been harvested and were either being driven to factories or stored in the fields and covered.
Sugar beet deliveries to refineries on Nov 15 were 17.51 million tonnes, down from 17.56 million last year, the eighth weekly WVZ campaign report showed.

While this marked the first decline versus last year since the campaign started two months ago, the average sugar content at delivery had risen on the week and was well ahead of last year at 18.14 percent versus 16.73.
Sugar content at delivery on Nov 8 was 18.08 percent, up from 16.71 percent a year earlier, when the delivered beet volume was 15.24 million tonnes, compared with 15.12 million a year earlier.
WVZ runs delivery updates until the end of the campaign in January on a weekly basis.
